summary.text: A 60-year-old Black male with HIV infection on HAART, HIV encephalopathy and hyperthyroidism, and no previous lung disease or active smoking, presented with worsening confusion, cough and generalized weakness. On examination he was frail, tachycardic and had scattered rhonchi; initial blood pressure was 95/77 mmHg, heart rate 110 beats/min and oxygen saturation 97% on room air.

Workup showed leukocytosis and elevated D-dimer, ESR, CRP and LDH, an undetectable HIV viral load, a negative serum beta-D-glucan, and bilateral parenchymal infiltrates on chest x-ray. SARS-CoV-2 PCR was positive, hydroxychloroquine was started, and HAART was continued throughout the admission. Febrile episodes occurred during the hospital course.

On the fourth day of admission worsening dyspnea led to a repeat chest x-ray showing bilateral 20% apical pneumothoraces without tension. He was transferred to the intensive care unit on a non-rebreather mask, where oxygen saturation dropped to 85% and a left-sided tension pneumothorax was found. A chest tube was placed, oxygen requirements kept rising, and he was intubated and ventilated. On day 9 CT and CTA showed a left pneumothorax of 10% of hemithorax volume and ruled out pulmonary embolism.

On hospital day 18, after remaining hemodynamically stable, the pneumothorax was reabsorbed and he was extubated and moved to the inpatient medical floor. He was discharged in stable condition breathing on room air 11 days later.
